" the standard epoch"

That was the standard epoc for the PC world as implemented by IBM on the first PC. Unix ran on big iron and existed in a different world. What you're seeing is an artifact of a BIOS compatibility mode. And, yes, it's stupid to still have that 34 years later.

It's not HP -- That's the old DOS/BIOS default date. That was the date every PC (IBM 5150) would boot into. There was no built-in RTC. You'd have to set the date and time at every boot. Most people had 'date' in their autoexec.bat files to prompt for it.

They ensure they have decent employees through various methods. Its nearly impossible to get hired on directly, you usually have to be a temp first unless you have some kind of skill they need (engineers for example) and their turnover rate for permanent employees is VERY low.
